page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head at top centre. Page number at top right. No marginal notes. Signature and catchword at the foot, right.

main_text.p: eft, sibi consulendi, hoc est, res suas augendi & stabiliendi cupiditas. Quod.n. vna quaeque illarum suis viribus sese obtinere posse desperat, id vel alienis opibus & auxiliis assequi studet. Haec autem vt impetrare possit, sua quoque aliis officia prolixe defert:interim res suas, non communes, potissimum respiciens & agens.

§. Cauffae προκαταρκτικά pro diuerfitate ob-iectorum variant. Interdum vicinae gentis successus, opes & iniuriae, aemulationi ansam praebent: sic vt in ordinem redigendae videantur. Vt Croesus mouit bellum, qui Persas & Medos florere animaduerteret, sibiq; adiunxit Athenienses & Lacedaemonios aliosq; populos, vt Herodotus in Clio testatur.

Nonnunquam impiae gentes, halcedo-nia Ecclesiae inuidentes, conspirant aduersus eam, vt docent elegantes illae hypoty-poses in Psalmis multis, potissimum vero 46.48.79.83. In hoc postremo Psalm. verf.§, dicitur. Dixerunt, Venite & succidamus eos de gente, & ne memoretur nomen Israel vltra.6. Quoniam consilium inierunt pariter, contra te foedus pepigerunt, &c.
4. Finis confoederationis est, vt sua quaeque gens rem agat, adiuta alienis opibus & viribus. Ex eo autem facile est colligere,

page.notes: Greek word after "Cauffae" is hard to read at this scan resolution; transcribed as printed as far as visible. Section mark after "verf." and the final "6." after "vltra" are uncertain. "quū" in the Croesus sentence is a doubtful abbreviation. Catchword and signature at the foot are faint. Printed spelling kept, including "defert:interim", "Quod.n." and the "ob-" and "halcedo-" line-end hyphens. Long s rendered as s throughout.
